messages:
sarah: CI deploy failing intermittently to staging — runner logs show 'PermissionDenied: service account impersonation: delegation window expired'. Happens ~10% of runs. Anyone seen this? @raj @devops-bot

raj: Can you paste the exact error blob and the pipeline job ts so I can correlate with runner logs?

sarah: paste from job log:
```
deploy-step: invoking gcloud
$ gcloud iam service-accounts generate-access-token \
  --impersonate-service-account=ci-deployer@redwood-inference-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
ERROR: (gcloud) 403 Permission denied: Service account impersonation failed: delegation window exceeded (delegationExpiry: 2026-03-01T12:34:56Z)
```

devops-bot: Runner info: gitlab-runner:15.7, oidc-provider=gitlab.com, id_token TTL=60s, oidc helper v0.9.3, runner configured with token cache enabled.

raj: Two likely spots: 1) the GitLab-issued id_token is short-lived and we attempt the GCP STS/impersonation after it expired, or 2) clock skew between runner and STS leading to 'delegation window' check failure. Is the exchange happening in the same job step or across stages?

sarah: It's across stages — we mint id_token in build stage, store in artifact, then use it in deploy stage. Sometimes deploy stage starts >60s later due to queueing. Explains intermittent nature.

ben: That matches. Workarounds: - Refresh id_token right before exchange (preferred) - Increase id_token TTL in GitLab OIDC settings (if possible) - Avoid storing raw short-lived tokens in artifacts between stages.

raj: Also add resilient checks in the helper: if STS exchange returns delegation expiry, re-request id_token and retry once. We should add a small clock skew tolerance when validating delegationExpiry on our side.

sarah: I just pushed a pipeline patch: pre-deploy step now forces id_token refresh and we disabled token artifact caching for that job. Patch: https://gitlab.redwood/infra/pipelines/12345 (runs now).

devops-bot: Created INC-4321 and linked gitlab MR. Noted impacted customers: internal staging only.

raj: Long-term: consider issuing a delegated CI service account for cross-project deploys with a slightly longer impersonation window, or use Workload Identity Federation with direct pod-level tokens (no artifact caching). But ensure least-privilege — only allow impersonation for the dedicated deployer SA.

ben: For immediate mitigation, I've updated the runner helper to refresh when cached token age >30s. Will roll in canary to three runners.

sarah: After the change two pipeline runs succeeded. I'll monitor for 24h then close. Thanks all :thumbsup:

raj: I'll draft a short ops note on 'OIDC token caching pitfalls' and include recommended pipeline patterns.

sarah: closing thread if no more incidents.
